memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The west end of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide and have curtains, with ten posts and ten bases. On the east end, toward the sunrise, the courtyard shall also be fifty cubits wide. Curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases, and curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on the other side, with three posts and three bases." - Exodus 27:12-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God specifies the courtyard's remaining sides, and notice which direction gets the entrance: the east, toward the sunrise. Every morning, the first light would fall on the way in. The design itself faced the dawn.

There is something fitting about that. God's dwelling was oriented toward new beginnings. Each sunrise found the entrance already turned toward the light, ready for another day of worshippers coming near. Lamentations tells us that God's mercies are new every morning, and great is His faithfulness (Lam 3:22-23). The way to Him opens fresh with each dawn.

If yesterday went badly — if you failed, drifted, or simply ran out of strength — the entrance still faces the sunrise. God is not waiting at the door with folded arms, tallying your record. His compassions do not wear out. The invitation to come near is renewed as reliably as the morning light. Whatever weight you are carrying from yesterday, you can bring it to Him today and find fresh mercy waiting. Turn toward the dawn.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I carrying yesterday's failures as though God's mercy has run out?
How would today look if I truly believed His mercies are new this morning?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, Your mercies are new every morning and Your faithfulness never fails. Thank You that the way to You is open again today. I bring You yesterday's weight and receive fresh grace. Amen.
